attempts.text: [{"name": "item_peak_lifecycle", "idea": "Lifecycle position of an item: its distinct users in the last 30 steps relative to its best 30-step bucket ever, plus how many buckets ago that peak was, so the model can tell rising items from fading ones independent of absolute popularity.", "level": "item", "sql": "WITH b AS (SELECT item_id, FLOOR(({A} - 1 - t) / 30) AS k, COUNT(*) AS c FROM ev GROUP BY 1, 2), p AS (SELECT item_id, k AS pk, c AS pc FROM (SELECT item_id, k, c, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY c DESC, k) AS rn FROM b) x WHERE rn = 1) SELECT p.item_id, CAST(COALESCE(b.c, 0) AS DOUBLE) / p.pc AS ag_peak_ratio, CAST(p.pk AS DOUBLE) AS ag_peak_age FROM p LEFT JOIN b ON b.item_id = p.item_id AND b.k = 0;"}, {"name": "item_pop_decay3", "idea": "Exponentially time-decayed audience over the last 30 steps with a 3-step scale, emphasizing the very latest demand more sharply than the fixed users_7 window.", "level": "item", "sql": "SELECT item_id, SUM(CASE WHEN t >= {A} - 30 THEN EXP(-({A} - 1 - t) / 3.0) ELSE 0 END) AS ag_pop_decay3 FROM ev GROUP BY item_id;"}, {"name": "cond_prob_decay_lift", "idea": "Directional co-occurrence P(j|i) over 180 steps summed over the user's up to 15 items of the last 60 steps with exponential recency weights, plus the maximum lift co(i,j)*N/(n(i)n(j)), giving normalizations that differ from the cosine scores.", "level": "pair", "sql": "WITH e AS (SELECT user_id, item_id FROM ev WHERE t >= {A} - 180), lu AS (SELECT user_id, item_id, t FROM (SELECT user_id, item_id, t, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY t DESC, item_id) AS rn FROM ev WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM users) AND t >= {A} - 60) x WHERE rn <= 15), src AS (SELECT DISTINCT item_id FROM lu), ni AS (SELECT item_id, COUNT(*) AS c FROM e GROUP BY item_id), nu AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS n FROM e), co AS (SELECT a.item_id AS i, b.item_id AS j, COUNT(*) AS c FROM e a JOIN e b ON a.user_id = b.user_id AND a.item_id <> b.item_id WHERE a.item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM src) GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT c.user_id, c.item_id, SUM(EXP(-({A} - lu.t) / 20.0) * CAST(co.c AS DOUBLE) / n1.c) AS ag_cond_decay, MAX(CAST(co.c AS DOUBLE) * nu.n / (CAST(n1.c AS DOUBLE) * n2.c)) AS ag_lift_max FROM cand c JOIN lu ON lu.user_id = c.user_id JOIN co ON co.i = lu.item_id AND co.j = c.item_id JOIN ni n1 ON n1.item_id = co.i JOIN ni n2 ON n2.item_id = co.j CROSS JOIN nu GROUP BY 1, 2;"}, {"name": "user_recency_ratio", "idea": "Recency relative to the user's own rhythm: steps since the last activity times the number of active-step gaps divided by the active span, so a long pause is judged against the user's usual inter-visit gap.", "level": "user", "sql": "WITH s AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, t FROM ev WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM users)) SELECT user_id, CAST({A} - MAX(t) AS DOUBLE) * (COUNT(*) - 1) / GREATEST(MAX(t) - MIN(t), 1) AS ag_recency_ratio FROM s GROUP BY user_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;"}, {"name": "adopter_depth", "idea": "Breadth of appeal: the mean ln(total items) of the item's adopters in the last 90 steps, since items taken by light users tend to be broadly appealing while items driven by heavy users are niche.", "level": "item", "sql": "WITH un AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM ev GROUP BY user_id) SELECT e.item_id, AVG(LN(un.n)) AS ag_adopter_depth FROM ev e JOIN un ON un.user_id = e.user_id WHERE e.t >= {A} - 90 GROUP BY e.item_id;"}]
